memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'For six years sow your fields, and for six years prune your vineyards
and gather their crops. But in the seventh year the land is to have a
year of sabbath rest, a sabbath to the LORD. Do not sow your fields or
prune your vineyards'" - Lev 25:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Six years of ordinary farming, and then a full year with no sowing and
no pruning. For a farming people, this was an enormous act of faith. An
entire year with no planting meant depending completely on what God
would provide.

Think of the anxiety it must have stirred. What if there is not enough?
What if we run out? God was deliberately building a nation that had to
trust Him with its food, not merely its worship.

Dear reader, it is easy to trust God with the abstract and hard to trust
Him with the practical. We say we believe He provides, yet we quietly
arrange our lives so that we never actually have to find out.

The seventh year removed that safety net once every seven years. It
forced the question: do we really believe our provision comes from God?

Jesus pointed to the same truth. He said, do not worry about your life,
what you will eat or drink. Look at the birds; your heavenly Father feeds
them. Are you not much more valuable (Matt 6:25-26)?

This is not a promise of wealth. It is an invitation to rest in a Father
who provides. Where is God asking you to stop striving and trust Him?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do I say I trust God but arrange things so I never have to?
2. What would it look like to genuinely depend on His provision?
3. Is worry about provision stealing my peace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for trusting my own arrangements more than Your care.
Teach me to depend on You for daily provision without anxiety. Amen.
